executiveSummary: GM0677's identity, Zeeland safety-region assignment, full 2025 boundary and CBS resident control are coherent. Fresh context reports 27,378 residents; 48 published neighbourhood rows sum to 27,380 (+2, +0.007%), a negligible difference that preserves CBS rounding and suppression semantics. The bundle contains fifteen districts, 48 neighbourhoods, fifteen BAG places, 60 BRT settlement labels and 59 scheduled-transit stop areas, but no rail station. All ten canonical presets execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services and pass structural and numerical contracts. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Hulst is a rural, Belgian-border municipality behind primary Westerschelde defences with distinct polders, drainage systems, villages and combustible woodland. The coastal preset reports 1,948 affected and severe mobility degradation at T+24 while direct inundation stress remains zero and no Westerschelde surge, defence, breach, coupure or polder case is selected. Eight unrelated hazards reuse exactly the same full neighbourhood severity order. A controlled ignition inside the official Waterwingebied St-Jansteen polygon leaves its containing Buitengebied Clinge only 33rd of 48. The logical graph has only two road clips toward Terneuzen, omitting N290's Belgian-border continuation and incident-valid tunnel, bridge, transit, care, supply and mutual-aid routes. Public water assets, grid planning, antennas, schools, care pages, observations and plans remain contextual rather than live topology or commitments. Missing municipal records are Unknown/NoData, never zero or safe.

evidenceSources.title: E01 — Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025, table 86165NED, OData API
supports: The official municipality row identifies GM0677 Hulst and reports 27,378 residents, density 136 per square kilometre, 27.5% age 65 or older and 4,583 one-person households.

The 48 published neighbourhood rows sum to 27,380 residents (+2, +0.007%), 12,950 households and 7,510 residents aged 65 or older. The small difference retains annual rounding and suppression semantics.

Average-home values cover 42/48 rows, cars per household 39/48, disability/AOW/assistance 43/48 and doctor/supermarket distance 47/48; district-heating share and public-charging counts cover zero rows and must not become zero.

CBS OData is machine-readable under CC BY 4.0, with quarterly additions described for this annual table. It controls resident allocation, not incident-time presence, disability, evacuation ability, injury or deprivation.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Full municipal geometry, settlements and road, rail and scheduled-transit reference inputs
evidenceSources.edition: 2025 boundary/statistics and current generated BAG, BRT, NWB, ProRail and GTFS reference snapshots
supports: The generated centre [4.089575446163689, 51.31125704898271] lies inside the fresh 2025 municipal boundary.
The bundle retains fifteen districts, 48 neighbourhoods, fifteen BAG places and 60 BRT labels: 23 woonkernen, four deelkernen, 26 gehuchten and seven buurtschappen.

The BAG label points for Kloosterzande and Ossenisse fall outside the generalized display boundary even though the places belong to GM0677; full geometry and administrative membership must govern inclusion rather than label-point clipping.

CBS boundary OGC is half-yearly/CC BY 4.0; BAG is daily/Public Domain Mark 1.0; BRT is CC BY 4.0; NWB is monthly/CC0 1.0; ProRail is manually refreshed/CC0 1.0. OVapi GTFS is free-use best-effort context without an operational SLA.
Nominal road values of 150 are scenario units; reference links and schedules do not prove direction, border continuity, passability, queue, accessible evacuation, incident capacity or operation.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Regionaal Crisisplan 2026–2029, legacy Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2020–2023 and current shelter/evacuation guidance
evidenceSources.edition: Crisis plan 2026–2029; publicly available risk profile 2020–2023 retained as expired historical baseline; current Zeelandveilig guidance
supports: The current strategic crisis plan coordinates with neighbouring Dutch safety regions and Belgian provinces; tactical incident and disaster plans, operational handbooks and maps sit below it. The public plan is governance evidence, not an operational resource or live-state feed.

The latest public regional risk profile located is explicitly the expired 2020–2023 edition. It prioritizes sea flooding, nuclear installations, hazardous-material transport, societal disruption/cyber and other utility, storm and nature-fire risks; it must be displayed as a historical planning baseline rather than current event state.

Current public guidance distinguishes evacuation from sheltering, advises closing doors/windows and ventilation when sheltering, moving high during flooding, anticipating traffic congestion and helping vulnerable people.

Zeeland's iodine guidance distinguishes distance/age/pregnancy groups around Borssele and Doel and says tablets are taken only on government instruction based on a release and wind. It supports a cross-border nuclear action protocol, not a current release, dose, zone assignment or blanket instruction.
These human-readable sources have publication/validity context but no stable public incident-resource API, operational cadence or stated blanket reuse licence.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Scheldestromen / Rijkswaterstaat Watermanagementcentrum Nederland / IPLO / Het Waterschapshuis
evidenceSources.title: E04 — Scheldestromen 2025 work and water-defence services, Kruispolder and drainage projects, and LIWO 2025.1.6
evidenceSources.edition: Scheldestromen 2025 feature services and programme material; LIWO release 2025.1.6
supports: The official 2025 service publishes primary and regional water barriers, primary/secondary/tertiary waters, pumps and related managed objects. A separate water-defence service publishes barriers, norm trajectories, gates, culverts, pumping stations and sluices; the service responses inspected do not state a reuse licence, so no licence is inferred.

The Kruispolder project places the Hulst polder system behind the Westerschelde sea dike and names Boudeloo/Kruispolder dikes, Walsoorden and Paal pumps, weirs, culverts and watercourses between Lamswaarde, Vogelkreek, Mariapolder and Graauw.

Scheldestromen's 2025 programme identifies Ossenisse surface-water return into sewer as a pumping-system load and names Kloosterzande runoff and Heikant drainage measures. These are local system evidence, not live control or guaranteed present capacity.

The deployment HWH/PDOK screen returns 153 points: fifteen sewer pumps, two wastewater-treatment points, ten surface-water pumps, one sluice and 125 weirs. Aggregation is partial and contributor-dependent under CC BY-SA 4.0 and does not establish connectivity, capacity, settings, power/backup or operation.

LIWO 2025.1.6 provides downloadable professional flood layers requiring specialist water-manager interpretation. A selected case must retain source/defence/failure, footprint, native units/resolution, arrival/persistence, probability, CRS, licence and NoData.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Official combustible-nature eligibility at Waterwingebied St-Jansteen and historical Hulst firefighting-water context
evidenceSources.edition: Risicokaart metadata updated 19 February 2026; St-Jansteen feature begins validity 6 December 2005; historical incident page 16 August 2025
supports: The official Public Domain WFS contains Waterwingebied St-Jansteen in GM0677, attributed to municipality Hulst and classified as mixed woodland. Its old feature-validity date must remain visible and does not establish current ignition or fuel condition.
The controlled audit origin [4.0768451379794, 51.257689182576655] lies inside this official polygon and CBS neighbourhood Buitengebied Clinge.

A Zeelandveilig report of a 16 August 2025 grass fire at Absdaalseweg, Hulst says a water tanker was required because nearby firefighting water was unavailable. It is a historical access/resource example, not current shortage or a prediction for St-Jansteen.
Eligibility and an incident report do not establish ignition, perimeter, fuel moisture, smoke, people present, access, current extinguishing-water availability, crews or suppression state.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — N290 Kapellebrug cross-border corridor and current Westerschelde/Sluiskil tunnel information
evidenceSources.edition: Province project reporting 2025 and current tunnel-operator information inspected September 2026
supports: Province Zeeland states that N290 connects N61/N62 through Zaamslag and Hulst to the Netherlands–Belgium border at Kapellebrug and carries traffic to Belgium. Its diversion discussion uses N290, Tractaatweg and E34.

The model's two municipal logical road records both terminate at Terneuzen and contain no Belgian boundary node, continuation or cross-border destination. This is a source-coverage omission, not proof that Belgian routes are unavailable.

The Westerscheldetunnel operator publishes current status for the Westerschelde and Sluiskil tunnels and approach roads. For planned Sluiskiltunnel closures it publishes fixed U64/U65 diversion via the bridge, demonstrating that tunnel state and a specific alternate route matter.

Project and operator webpages do not provide a blanket machine reuse licence or complete 72-hour route-capacity API. Retrieval-time status must carry issue/valid time, confirmation and expiry rather than being assumed indefinitely.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Hulst ambulance and residential-care locations, 24/7 acute-care referral to Terneuzen and national accessibility context
evidenceSources.edition: Current provider pages and RIVM 2024 acute-care accessibility analysis
supports: ZorgSaam publishes ambulance posts at Hulst, Terneuzen and Oostburg and says most patients go to De Honte in Terneuzen. It notes that posts may not be sufficiently staffed during busy periods and names temporary coverage locations including Vogelwaarde.

ZorgSaam's emergency department at De Honte is open 24/7. Provider pages also list care locations in Hulst, Kloosterzande and Sint Jansteen, establishing local care and cross-boundary access dependencies without exposing incident-time occupancy or capacity.

RIVM's 2024 accessibility analysis classifies De Honte as sensitive for 56,100 residents in that annual model. This older model result is planning context, not live acceptance or a GM0677-specific forecast.

The deployment's 2026 v1.1 RIVM acute-care screen returns no point inside GM0677. That spatial match is NoData for an in-boundary acute-care facility, consistent with referral to Terneuzen; it is not zero care demand, ambulance coverage or accessible capacity.
Provider webpages have no machine-readable live staffing/acceptance/backup/restoration contract or stated machine reuse licence; RIVM acute-care data are annual under CC0 1.0.

Zeeland's KNMI warning snapshot reports level zero at retrieval and no KNMI observation is assigned inside GM0677. A provincial warning is issue-time context with a short window, not gridded local forcing or an all-clear for arbitrary exercises.

No GM0677 Waterinfo observation/forecast, NDW situation, RIVM acute-care point, PM2.5 station or KNMI seismic event is assigned. Sparse point/register matching is a coverage fact; absence remains Unknown rather than zero hazard, disruption, pollution or care need.

NBNL planning/queue context updates at least quarterly/monthly but the frontend endpoint and exact licence are not a stable dataset contract. RDI cadence/licence is unstated; DUO is daily under CC Attribution version unspecified; KNMI is ten-minute/CC BY 4.0; RIVM acute care is annual/CC0 1.0; Waterinfo and NDW are CC0 unless stated. All remain affectsSimulation=false context.

findings.summary: The coastal preset reports affected residents and severe mobility loss but zero inundation stress without a selected Westerschelde defence case.
findings.evidence: Scheldestromen data and Kruispolder documentation identify the Westerschelde sea dike, primary/regional barriers, norm trajectories, sluices, pumps, culverts and named polder systems. Yet coastal T+24 reports severity 0.031769, 1,948 affected, Mobility 0.326565 and Supply 0.564169 while normalized inundation stress is exactly zero. No surge level, defence/coupure/failure, polder footprint, arrival or persistence explains the result. River exact zero is only the scoped direct-river output and cannot imply safety from estuarine/coastal flooding, rainfall/drainage or external cascades. The field is normalized stress, not metres.
findings.action: Suppress exact local coastal/river impacts until an authority-selected LIWO/Scheldestromen/RWS case supplies source, water level, defence/coupure/failure/control state, footprint, native units/resolution, arrival/persistence, probability, CRS, issue/valid time, licence, NoData, transform hash and reviewer. Separate direct inundation from wind, mobility, supply and external effects; Unknown is not safe.

findings.summary: An explicit ignition inside official Waterwingebied St-Jansteen leaves its containing neighbourhood 33rd of 48.
findings.evidence: Risicokaart identifies Waterwingebied St-Jansteen as combustible mixed woodland. Audit point [4.0768451379794, 51.257689182576655] is inside that polygon and Buitengebied Clinge. At T+11/T+24 fire is 0.355010, smoke 0.456431 and municipal severity 0.397535, yet the containing neighbourhood ranks 33/48 while Zoetevaart ranks first. The origin is controlled, not an actual fire. A historical Hulst grass fire also demonstrates that local extinguishing-water access can matter but does not prove current state.
findings.action: Block local fire ranking from operational use. Require source/perimeter intersection with full neighbourhood and versioned combustible polygons, plus issue-valid wind/humidity, fuel moisture, people present, access, extinguishing water, crews and suppression state. Preserve old feature dates and render absent current ignition as Unknown.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated hazards reuse one complete neighbourhood order across coastal polders, border woodland, villages and Hulst town.

Official sources distinguish Westerschelde barriers/polders, named drainage systems, St-Jansteen woodland, border/road/tunnel routes, settlements and service domains. Cyber and heat have no defensible reason to share fire and rainfall rank.
findings.action: Replace the municipality seed with hazard-specific source, eligible-domain, forcing, exposed-object and evidence-support adapters. Require cross-preset tests that unrelated hazards do not silently share a full order; missing compatible spatial support must show Unknown rather than precise ranking.

residualLimitations: Complete physical electricity, gas, drinking-water, sewer/drainage, telecom, care and supply topology, live load, outage, backup, crews, spares, fuel and restoration state are unavailable or security-sensitive. Public geometry, plans and registers cannot replace them.

No selected LIWO/Scheldestromen/RWS hydraulic case establishes a GM0677 Westerschelde surge, defence/coupure/failure footprint, polder propagation or arrival/persistence. A generic result is not evidence, and a zero does not prove safety.

The 2020–2023 regional risk profile is expired and retained only as a public historical baseline. The 2026–2029 crisis plan is strategic governance evidence rather than a live resource or tactical-state feed.

Risicokaart establishes static combustible eligibility only. It does not establish ignition, fuel moisture, perimeter, people present, access, extinguishing water or suppression; the St-Jansteen source is an audit fixture.
The 2025 Absdaalseweg fire report is a historical resource/access example, not evidence of a present fire, current water shortage or future incident behaviour.

CBS residents omit pupils, patients, care residents, visitors, seasonal/temporary workers, border/road users and responders. Aggregate age/household statistics cannot identify personal vulnerability or incident-time presence.

ZorgSaam and RIVM pages do not expose incident-time ambulance staffing, hospital acceptance, care occupancy, backup or restoration; protected operational information must not be reconstructed publicly.
NWB, GTFS and tunnel/project pages do not prove scenario-time road, border, tunnel, bridge or bus service, emergency priority, accessibility, detours, destination or throughput.

One Stedin planning postcode has null core capacity values; its queue and projects do not establish live local topology, capacity, outage or restoration. RDI antennas, DUO schools and water objects likewise remain affectsSimulation=false without reviewed causal bindings.
A level-zero warning and no municipally assigned KNMI observation, Waterinfo, NDW, PM2.5, acute-care or seismic point are coverage/time facts, not zero hazard, disruption, pollution or care need.

Nuclear/radiological and hazardous-material plume hazards are not represented by the ten canonical presets. Public shelter, evacuation, ventilation and iodine guidance cannot be activated without an authoritative incident and order.

Exact hazard, affected-population, service, recovery and person-hour outputs remain synthetic exercise results, not observations, official forecasts, operator commitments or decision-grade advice until critical/high findings are corrected and authorities review the case.
This audit covers only the first 72 hours. Flood displacement, pollution, care interruption, agricultural impacts and infrastructure recovery can persist much longer.
